clinician.final_diagnosis: Cytomegalovirus retinitis with a macular star in an immunocompetent individual
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old man presented with diminished vision in the right eye (hand movement) and left eye (6/60) five months after right eye trauma. The right eye showed a traumatic cataract with normal B-scan; the left eye showed sluggish pupillary reaction. Left eye fundus examination revealed a large (~0.5 DD) white fluffy necrotizing lesion with overlying retinal hemorrhages, scattered necrotic spots along the inferotemporal arcade, mild optic disc pallor with grade 1 edema, and a macular star located ~2DD from the optic disc (E001). OCT confirmed hyperreflective signals at the outer plexiform layer representing retinal exudates (E001). Laboratory workup confirmed immunocompetence with negative HIV serology, normal CD4 count of 950 cells/mm3, and negative hepatitis B and C (E002). Serology showed elevated CMV IgG (1073 AU/ml) with normal IgM, indicating prior CMV exposure (E002). Extensive workup excluded toxoplasmosis (IgM negative), syphilis (FTA-ABS, VDRL), tuberculosis (PPD, chest X-ray), sarcoidosis (ACE), and autoimmune etiologies (ANA, RF, antiphospholipid antibody) (E002). The patient failed initial empiric therapy with prednisolone 60mg/day and Septran DS BID (E003). He was then started on valganciclovir (900mg daily for 21 days, then 450mg daily for 6 weeks) with prednisolone taper (E003). At 1.5 months follow-up, left eye vision improved to 6/6 with healing choroiditis patch, resolving hemorrhagic patch, and resolving macular star (E004). Repeat serology showed decreased CMV IgG titers (159 AU/ml) (E005).
